new: The performance run: the headset plays every story and the studio's example scenes by itself, chapter by chapter, and measures every frame. About 75 minutes; #perfrun&prch=10 takes about 45.
Its hands-on part: about five minutes of one card at a time (the panel, the menu, the grip, the sticks, walking, occlusion, the Stories screen, a studio scene), each with Done and Skip.
To start either in a headset: turn developer mode on, then open the address with #perfrun (or #handson), or use the Performance run and Hands-on test rows on the menu's Debug tab.
The results stay on the headset and, with developer mode on, go to the relay as a run log; node tools/notes/notes.mjs perfrun <id> turns one into a table, or compares two.
A pause of a second or more now counts in the numbers, and a page's display rate is measured once before the run, not guessed from a slow story.
test: On a Quest: start the run-through with #perfrun in VR and let it finish; the results card should show and the run log reach the relay.
The hands-on part: press Done on some cards and Skip on others.
Run it on two headsets and compare the two runs with notes.mjs perfrun.
Stop a run from the Debug tab, also while a story is loading: it should stop at once and put automatic quality back.
Take the headset off mid-run, put it back on and Enter VR: the run should go on from where it stopped.
Any two stories in VR and one in AR: everything looks as before, in stereo (v228's eye lock); the exposome story stays put.
untested: Everything of the performance run in a real headset: a session of over an hour, the battery, the cards' comfort, every hands-on step and the numbers themselves.
The lock on the eye cameras was tried only with a pretend headset: that it changes nothing in the picture on a Quest is untested.
Everything in a headset since v220 except calibration, which the owner tried on v226.
